doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The happy Basie trumpet section of Thad, Joe Newman and Albert Aarons
summary: Young lists the later Basie four-trumpet section and says a section that likes each other plays well.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So when you were with Count Basie you felt that everybody was there for everybody?
That was a happy band. That band that I‘m talking about, the last band…
No, you‘re talking about the last band with Count Basie.
Yeah, Count Basie…the five trumpets was Thad Jones, me, Wendell Cully passed so they got…who did they get in place of him? They didn‘t have five trumpets.
Yeah, they had four trumpets in Basie‘s band, right.
And…what‘s that trumpet player that used to? Albert Aarons. Albert Aarons— double ‗a‘, Albert Aarons. Myself…
Joe Newman, Thad, Albert Aarons…Thad four.
That was a good trumpet section. They worked together good, when musicians like one another and can talk, that was a good trumpet section.
